patterns.key_values: notch-morph opaque-black rounded panel (~28-34px bottom radius), header row (status glyph + title/subtitle + trailing gear) over hairline divider over 3 equal-width metric columns split by vertical hairlines
notch-mounted utility; transient reminder pill emerges from the notch (bold-white title left + pixel-art metric glyph right), full dashboard drops down
metric column = colored glyph + tracked-uppercase label + large white value (X/Y) + capsule colored progress bar on dark track; value-dominant label/value hierarchy

signature_moves: The notch IS the product surface — reminders emerge as pills and the dashboard drops from the physical notch; opaque true-black chosen to fuse with the bezel (glass would break the illusion); 'right where you already look'
8-bit arcade theme carried edge to edge — pixel-heart icon, pixel-dot 'mood face' status glyph, pixel-art banner glyphs (equalizer, dot-matrix droplet) — warmth/whimsy vs clinical health gauges
Per-metric identity hue (cyan water / green breaks / orange movement / mint balance) with value-large-white, label-small-gray — Activity-ring logic without rings, hue always paired with glyph+label
Humane personified micro-voice ('Thirsty yet?', 'Move that body', 'before it starts complaining') softening interruption
defects: Tracked-uppercase micro-labels (mild non-native tell) — WATER/BREAKS/MOVEMENT are letter-spaced caps; web/iOS-widget convention where AppKit uses sentence-case; systematic + compact-purposeful so reads as genre styling, but leans further from native than its notch-genre peers
Contrast Dilution (non-text, minor) — hairline dividers (~8%) and progress tracks (~10%) sit below the 3:1 non-text floor; intentional recession

aesthetic.direction: Playful/toy crossed with Terminal/hacker — an '8-bit health HUD': black ground, pixel-art glyphs, neon identity accents; a themed remix, not a template default

psychology: Fitts's Law + information scent — mounting at the notch (top-center, where cursor/eyes already rest) minimizes travel to the info; the app literally states 'right where you already look'
Jakob's Law — borrows the iPhone Dynamic Island schema (pill morphs from the notch) so users already know how to read it
Goal-Gradient / Zeigarnik — X/Y progress framing (1.2/2L, 4/6, 5/8) and colored bars nag incomplete goals toward completion
Von Restorff / signal detection — neon value numbers pop against pure black for peripheral glanceability
Aesthetic-Usability effect — pixel-art warmth makes a nagging health tool feel friendly, buying forgiveness for interruptions
Hick's Law (respected) — only 3 metrics + 2 quiet actions on the panel; minimal choice at a glance
Tension (not seen in static): peripheral motion at the notch could hijack attention during deep work; app mitigates rhetorically with 'quiet nudge' copy
notes: Only shot-2 is a (near-)full app surface; shot-3/shot-4 carry a genuine notch banner in the top strip over a marketing composite; cover/shot-1 are marketing composites with NO app UI (brand evidence only). All renders are 1270x760 at indeterminate scale — every pt value is estimated with wide ranges; trust proportions/hierarchy over absolute sizes. Lineage runtime is confidently native (notch-morph overlay is native-only) but the visible grammar is fully custom-drawn and must not feed macOS native canon (lineage gate). Fits the corpus's emerging notch-hud/dynamic-island genre (Alcove, DynamicLake, Claude Notch Usage Companion) but differentiates via retro-pixel theme. meta.json has no long_description; tagline 'Work shouldn't cost you your health' is marketing context, not design evidence.
